items.q: Look! The lion dance team ______ down our street right now.
items.vi: Nhìn kìa! Đội múa lân đang đi xuống phố nhà mình ngay lúc này.
items.explanation: An action happening at the moment of speaking (Look!, right now) takes the present continuous: is coming; the present simple, present perfect and past simple do not describe what is going on now.

items.q: In the south of Viet Nam, the rainy ______ usually lasts from May to November.
items.vi: Ở miền Nam Việt Nam, mùa mưa thường kéo dài từ tháng Năm đến tháng Mười Một.
items.explanation: A season is a part of the year with its own weather; a term is part of a school year, an era is a long period of history, and a decade is ten years.

items.q: The forecast says a ______ wind will blow from the north tonight, so bring a jacket.
items.vi: Dự báo nói tối nay sẽ có gió mạnh thổi từ phía bắc, nên hãy mang theo áo khoác.
items.explanation: Wind is strong (or light); heavy goes with rain and traffic, thick with fog, and large does not describe wind.

items.q: Since Mai joined the school drama club, she has really ______ — she chats with everyone now.
items.vi: Từ khi Mai vào câu lạc bộ kịch của trường, bạn ấy thật sự đã cởi mở hơn hẳn — giờ bạn ấy trò chuyện với tất cả mọi người.
items.explanation: To come out of your shell is to stop being shy and start talking to people. Come to your senses is to start thinking sensibly, come down to earth is to become realistic, and come full circle is to return to where something started.

items.q: The tour guide ______ that the old market had been rebuilt after the fire.
items.vi: Hướng dẫn viên chỉ ra rằng khu chợ cũ đã được xây lại sau vụ cháy.
items.explanation: To point out is to tell people a fact they may not have noticed. Point at needs a thing you aim your finger at, turn out is used with it (it turned out that…), and leave out means to omit.

items.q: The streets are completely dry this morning, so it ______ last night.
items.vi: Sáng nay đường phố khô ráo hoàn toàn, nên tối qua chắc chắn là không mưa.
items.explanation: Can't have + past participle expresses a confident conclusion that something did NOT happen in the past; must have would mean the opposite, and should have and might rain do not fit the dry-street evidence.

items.q: There will be a fifteen-minute ______ between the two water-puppet shows, so you can buy some snacks.
items.vi: Sẽ có mười lăm phút giải lao giữa hai suất múa rối nước, nên bạn có thể mua chút đồ ăn vặt.
items.explanation: A planned break between two parts of a show is an interval; a delay is unplanned lateness, a recess is a break at school or in court, and an era is a long period of history.

items.q: The bus ______ Nam takes to school every morning was twenty minutes late again today.
items.vi: Chiếc xe buýt mà Nam đi học mỗi sáng hôm nay lại trễ hai mươi phút.
items.explanation: The relative pronoun refers to a thing (the bus) and is the object of takes, so which (or that) is used; who is for people, whose shows possession, and where would need a complete clause after it.

items.q: Very ______ pupils remembered to bring their raincoats, so most of them got soaked on the way home.
items.vi: Rất ít học sinh nhớ mang áo mưa, nên hầu hết các em bị ướt sũng trên đường về nhà.
items.explanation: Few means 'almost no', stressing how small the number is, and it is the only option that can follow very; a few means 'some' (very a few is impossible), while little and a little go with uncountable nouns, not pupils.

items.q: Lan ______ the lantern festival three times since she moved to Hoi An.
items.vi: Từ khi chuyển đến Hội An, Lan đã đi lễ hội đèn lồng ba lần.
items.explanation: Since + a past point and three times describe experience up to now, so the present perfect has visited is needed; the past simple and past perfect cut the link with the present.

items.q: On the way to the beach, Dad stopped ______ some petrol at the station near the bridge.
items.vi: Trên đường ra biển, bố dừng lại để mua xăng ở cây xăng gần cầu.
items.explanation: Stop to do means to pause in order to do something else: Dad stopped the car so that he could buy petrol. Stop doing would mean he gave up buying petrol, and a bare infinitive or past form cannot follow stop.

items.q: Please ______ your seat belt before the coach pulls out of the station.
items.vi: Vui lòng thắt dây an toàn trước khi xe khách rời bến.
items.explanation: You fasten (or do up) a seat belt; tie is for shoelaces and ropes, close for doors and windows, and fix means to repair or attach.

items.q: Uncle Tam is always ______: his bus leaves the depot at exactly six every morning.
items.vi: Bác Tâm lúc nào cũng đúng giờ: xe buýt của bác rời bến đúng sáu giờ mỗi sáng.
items.explanation: A punctual person does things at the right time; temporary means lasting a short while, recent means happening not long ago, and urgent means needing action at once.

items.q: There was a thunderstorm last night; ______, the morning market opened as usual.
items.vi: Tối qua có giông bão; tuy vậy, chợ sáng vẫn mở cửa như thường lệ.
items.explanation: The second clause contrasts with the first, so the linking adverb of contrast nevertheless is needed; therefore shows a result, moreover adds a point, and otherwise means 'if not'.

items.q: Somehow the whole class ______ Nam's surprise party, so it wasn't a surprise at all.
items.vi: Không hiểu sao cả lớp đã nghe phong thanh về bữa tiệc bất ngờ của Nam, nên nó chẳng còn bất ngờ chút nào.
items.explanation: To get wind of something is to hear about it, often by chance or before it is meant to be known. Get the hang of is to learn how to do something, get the better of is to defeat, and get rid of is to throw away.

items.q: If the weather office hadn't ruled out a storm, the boat race on the river ______.
items.vi: Nếu cơ quan khí tượng không loại trừ khả năng có bão thì cuộc đua thuyền trên sông đã bị hủy rồi.
items.explanation: The if-clause is past perfect (hadn't ruled out), a third conditional about an unreal past, so the main clause takes would have + past participle: would have been cancelled.

items.q: We reached the station ten minutes ______, so we had time for a coffee before the train left.
items.vi: Chúng tôi đến ga sớm mười phút, nên có thời gian uống cà phê trước khi tàu chạy.
items.explanation: Ten minutes early means before the planned time; soon means in a short time from now, lately means recently, and quickly describes speed, not time of arrival.

items.q: A number of lanterns ______ hung along the river every full-moon night in Hoi An.
items.vi: Nhiều chiếc đèn lồng được treo dọc bờ sông vào mỗi đêm rằm ở Hội An.
items.explanation: A number of + plural noun takes a plural verb (only the number of is singular), and every full-moon night calls for the present simple, so are hung.

items.q: At the meeting, the head girl ______ a plan for a greener school festival.
items.vi: Tại cuộc họp, bạn nữ đại diện học sinh đã đề xuất một kế hoạch cho lễ hội trường xanh hơn.
items.explanation: To put forward a plan or idea is to suggest it for discussion. Put off means to postpone, put away means to store, and put up means to build something or display a poster.

items.q: ______ from the top of the hill, the whole town looks like a toy model.
items.vi: Nhìn từ đỉnh đồi, cả thị trấn trông như một mô hình đồ chơi.
items.explanation: The town is seen (it does not do the seeing), so the past participle gives the passive meaning; Seeing or Having seen would need a subject who looks, and To see expresses purpose.

items.q: By next Tet, my family ______ in this town for exactly ten years.
items.vi: Đến Tết sang năm, gia đình tôi sẽ sống ở thị trấn này tròn mười năm.
items.explanation: By + a future time and for ten years describe an action completed up to a point in the future, so the future perfect will have lived is needed.

items.q: The old tram line closed years ago; ______ most people in the city take the metro.
items.vi: Tuyến tàu điện cũ đã đóng cửa nhiều năm trước; ngày nay hầu hết người dân thành phố đi tàu điện ngầm.
items.explanation: Nowadays means at the present time, in contrast with the past; lately needs the present perfect, and formerly and previously both refer to the past.

items.q: ______ gets to the bus stop first should save seats for the rest of the group.
items.vi: Ai đến trạm xe buýt trước thì nên giữ chỗ cho cả nhóm.
items.explanation: Whoever means 'the person who' and can be the subject of gets; whatever and whichever refer to things, and whom is an object form that cannot be a subject.

items.q: Tet ______ on a different date each year because it follows the lunar calendar.
items.vi: Tết rơi vào một ngày khác nhau mỗi năm vì nó theo lịch âm.
items.explanation: A festival or holiday falls on a date; drop, set and lie are not used with dates.

items.q: Let's go to the flower market on Sunday morning, ______?
items.vi: Sáng Chủ nhật mình đi chợ hoa nhé?
items.explanation: The question tag for Let's is always shall we; will you is the tag for an imperative, and do/don't we follow a present simple statement.
